facts.raw_span: purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet
dusky purpuric macules and patches on her nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear
reticulated purpuric macules and patches on her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms
skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL)
Acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL)
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels (cryocrit, 16%)
Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation

concepts.why: The patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi, which are characteristic of cryoglobulinemia.
The patient has an abnormal paraprotein band, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells, which are indicative of multiple myeloma.
The patient has purpuric lesions, dusky purpuric macules and patches, and reticulated purpuric macules and patches, which are characteristic of vasculitis.
The patient has elevated creatinine levels, which indicate acute kidney injury.

rationales.F01: Purpuric lesions are a common manifestation of cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F07: Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear is a characteristic finding in cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F08: Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses is a key feature of multiple myeloma and cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F09: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis is a specific finding in multiple myeloma and cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F10: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels are a diagnostic criterion for cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F12: Multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi is a characteristic histopathological finding in cryoglobulinemia.

frontier_selector.rationale: Multiple Myeloma best explains the hypercalcemia, abnormal paraprotein band, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and hypercellular marrow with atypical plasma cells, with Cryoglobulinemia being a possible complication
